idea-plugin.name: DevBeer
idea-plugin.description:
DevBeer — everyday developer tools, inside your IDE

A grab-bag of the small utilities you keep leaving the IDE for. No web tools, no pasting company config into a random online diff site, no context switch.

Property & YAML File Compare

Compare two configuration files key-by-key — .properties against .properties, YAML against YAML, or .properties against YAML, because both are flattened to the same dotted key space first.

  • Interactive table: every key with its left value, right value and status (identical, different, only on the left, only on the right).
  • Live filtering — search by key or value, or show only the differences.
  • Double-click any cell to jump straight to that key's line in the source file.
  • Open a normalized side-by-side view in the IDE's own diff editor, so YAML and .properties line up even when the original files look nothing alike.
  • Raw file diff in the same editor when you want the literal text comparison.
  • Options for case-insensitive and whitespace-insensitive value comparison.
  • Copy or save a report of the differences.
  • Right-click two files in the Project view → DevBeer | Compare Property Files.

Folder Compare

Compare two directory trees file by file — and, unlike a plain directory diff, it understands configuration files.

  • Every file with its size on each side and a status of identical, different, only left or only right.
  • For .properties and YAML pairs, an extra column says how they differ — “2 changed, 1 only left” — without opening anything.
  • Double-click a config file to open it in the key-level Property Compare; double-click anything else for the side-by-side diff.
  • Compares by content hash, not just size and timestamp. Turn contents off for a fast pass.
  • Skips build, target, node_modules, .git and friends by default.
  • Runs in the background and can be cancelled. Right-click two folders in the Project view → DevBeer | Compare Folders.

JSON Formatter

Format, minify and validate JSON, backed by a real parser rather than whitespace juggling — so broken input gets a reason and a position instead of mangled output.

  • Pretty print with 2 spaces, 4 spaces or tabs; minify; sort keys at every level.
  • Syntax errors report the reason with a line and column, and put the caret on it.
  • Lenient mode reads the JSON people actually write: // and /* */ comments, trailing commas and single-quoted strings.
  • Lossless — 1.0, 1e3 and duplicate keys survive a round trip instead of being quietly rewritten.
  • Right-click in the editor → Format JSON to reformat the selection, or the whole file, as one undoable change.

String Toolbox

74 text transformations with a live preview, in one tool window.

  • Case — camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, CONSTANT_CASE, kebab-case, dot.case, Title Case, Sentence case, swap case.
  • Encode / decode — Base64 (standard + URL-safe), URL, HTML entities, hex, Unicode escapes.
  • Hash — MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, CRC32.
  • JSON / XML — pretty print, minify, escape as a Java string, JWT decode.
  • Lines — sort, natural sort, reverse, deduplicate, trim, number, join, split, wrap for a SQL IN clause.
  • Config — convert .properties to YAML and back, flatten and sort keys.
  • Time / IDs — epoch ↔ ISO-8601, UUID generation.
  • Transform the current editor selection in place: right-click → Transform Selection…

Spring Boot Property Hints (Java IDEs only)

The original feature of this plugin, still here and improved. Resolved property values appear as inlay hints right next to the code:

  • @Value("${my.prop}") shows the value found in each profile's config file.
  • @ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "…") shows how many keys bind under the prefix, and each field in the class shows its own resolved value.
  • Relaxed binding aware — maxPoolSize matches max-pool-size, max_pool_size and maxpoolsize.
  • Falls back to the inline default in ${my.prop:fallback} when nothing is configured.

The compare, folder, JSON and string modules run in every JetBrains IDE. The Spring inlay hints load only when Java support is present.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.3.0

  • New: AI Assistant. A lightweight, repository-aware assistant — ask about the project, explain a selection, suggest an improvement, trace a call flow, and analyse an error down to its root cause and the exact line to fix. Works with a local model over HTTP (Ollama and anything speaking its API) or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
    Off by default — no network call is made until you configure a provider, and nothing else in DevBeer depends on it.
  • Private by design: the repository is never uploaded. Only a ranked, budgeted slice of context is sent — capped at 10 files and 50,000 characters — after generated folders and secret files are excluded and credential-shaped values are redacted. API keys live in the OS keychain.
  • Fixes are reviewable, never automatic: a suggested edit is validated against the current file, shown as a preview, and applied only on your click, as one undoable change.
  • Wider IDE support: now installs on 2023.1 and newer, down from 2024.1 in 2.1.0. The floor was measured against every build from 2021.3 up rather than inferred.

2.2.0

  • New: Folder Compare. Compare two directory trees file by file. For .properties and YAML pairs it also reports how the keys differ, and drilling in opens the key-level Property Compare rather than a text diff. Compares by content hash, runs in the background, and can be cancelled.
  • New: JSON Formatter tool window and a Format JSON editor action.
  • Improved: JSON handling is backed by a real parser now. Broken input reports a reason with a line and column instead of producing mangled output, and formatting is lossless — 1.0, 1e3 and duplicate keys are no longer quietly rewritten.
  • New transforms: lenient JSON pretty print, JSON sort keys, and JSON validate.

2.1.0

  • Renamed to DevBeer, with a new logo. Same plugin, same settings — nothing to reinstall.
  • Wider IDE support: now installs on 2023.3 and newer, up from 2024.1. 2023.3 is the earliest build that has the declarative inlay-hints API the Spring hints are built on.

2.0.0

The plugin became a multi-tool — a home for everyday developer utilities rather than a single-feature plugin. (Released under the name "Dev Utility".)

  • New: Property & YAML File Compare tool window, with an interactive key-by-key table, jump-to-source, and normalized/raw side-by-side diff in the IDE's diff editor.
  • New: String Toolbox tool window with 60+ transformations and live preview.
  • New: Transform Selection… editor action.
  • New: Tools menu and Project view actions.
  • Improved: The YAML reader is a real indentation parser now — nested maps, lists, multi-document files, block scalars and flow collections are all handled. The previous version silently missed most nested keys.
  • Improved: @ConfigurationProperties is actually implemented, including per-field hints and relaxed binding.
  • Improved: Property lookups are cached per project instead of re-scanning every config file on every inlay hint, which made large projects crawl.
  • Improved: Works in non-Java IDEs; Java support is now an optional dependency.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: Spring Boot @Value inlay hints.
